page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by KVM virtualization within the Enhanced family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs based on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This hardware allocation profile targets compute-heavy workloads requiring high processing capacity relative to system memory.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps, facilitating steady data transfer for networked applications. Storage capabilities rely entirely on network-attached block storage rather than ephemeral local disks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high ratio of dedicated processing cores to system memory provides concentrated compute capability without unnecessary memory overhead. The primary tradeoff is the 2.0 GB per vCPU RAM constraint, which limits suitability for memory-bound applications or large in-memory databases. Appropriate workloads include software compilation pipelines, batch processing jobs, compute-intensive web serving, and network security appliances.

The instance includes 10 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth but provides zero attached local storage and no GPU hardware accelerators. By concentrating compute capacity without excess memory overhead, the ecs.c6t.8xlarge offers an efficient profile for parallel processing workloads. The primary tradeoff is its constrained memory capacity per core, making it less suitable for memory-heavy datasets. It is well suited for software compilation, batch processing pipelines, web serving clusters, and compute-intensive enterprise applications relying on external storage solutions.
